newsitem.title: USA: Texas House panel unanimously approves tax plan.
newsitem.headline: Texas House panel unanimously approves tax plan.

text.p: A Texas House of Representatives panel Wednesday unanimously approved a tax overhaul plan that calls for a $1 billion net reduction in the property taxes Texans pay, a spokeswoman for the panel's chairman said Thursday.

The plan, approved by the 11-member house select committee on revenue and public education funding, would cut residential property tax rates by 50 percent on average, according to a spokeswoman for select committee chairman Rep. Paul Sadler, D-8.
The plan would cap residential tax rates at 70 cents per $100 of valuation and business' tax rates at $1.05 per $100 of valuation, the spokeswoman said.
The proposal also calls for the state to pay 80 percent of public education costs, and for an expansion of the sales tax base, she said.

"Instead of creating new taxes like (Gov. George Bush's) original plan had entailed, this one broadens the sales tax base because it repeals a lot of the exemptions that certain industries have had for years," the spokeswoman said.
The select committee was appointed for the current legislative session only, the spokeswoman said.

"The Speaker of the House invented this committee for this session, and it's the first time in Texas history that a representative has ever been chairman of two committees at one time, because he is also chairman of public education," she said.
Both House Speaker James Laney, a democrat, and Governor Bush, a republican, were on hand when the bill was voted out of committee, the spokeswoman said.
"And the governor is in full support of the plan," she said.
The plan now proceeds to the full house for a vote.
